newsitem.title: UK: Copper price undervalued but seen capped - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Copper price undervalued but seen capped - analyst.

text.p: Copper prices are undervalued based on supply/demand fundamentals but a recovery in 1997 is likely to be capped by several factors, Malcolm Southwood of J.B. Were and Son Ltd said on Monday.
"At the present time the price of copper seems largely divorced from the fundamentals," Southwood told a London Metal Exchange (LME) seminar.
"Total industry stocks are still very low at around 4.5 weeks' consumption. So we are quite confident in saying that copper is currently undervalued," Southwood said.
Southwood said the copper market has been close to balance so far in 1996 although a supply surplus was likely in 1997.
He forecast a surplus of 300,000 tonnes in 1997, while average cash prices on the LME would be around 86 cents per pound ($1,896/tonne).

Southwood said a number of factors would prevent a sustained price recovery for copper. They were - "Hedge selling" associated with unwinding Sumitomo positions. - LME warrants more readily available than for many months. - Large stock declines unlikely to continue beyond end-October. - Smelter capacity rising, causing the concentrates surplus to move downstream. - Electrowon (SX-EW) copper output rising rapidly.
"We believe that demand for copper will grow by a healthy three percent next year, but that this will be comfortably outpaced by supply growth," Southwood said.
